s.note: the casino lounge where Deloris sings
s.how: Simmer 24 cocktail franks for 3 minutes and drain. Warm 125ml barbecue sauce with 2 tbsp brown sugar and a splash of bourbon until bubbling and sticky. Toss the franks through the glaze, spear each with a toothpick and serve warm like a Reno lounge.

s.note: the choir's tea break after rehearsal
s.how: Rub 60g butter into 450g self-raising flour, then stir in 150g grated vintage cheddar, chopped chives and a pinch of cayenne. Mix in 300ml milk to a soft dough. Pat out, cut into rounds and bake at 220C for 12 minutes. Serve warm with butter.

m.note: the bland convent dinner Deloris can't believe
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck, then add 2 onions, crushed garlic, a spoon of smoked paprika and thyme. Pour in stock, a can of tomatoes and a splash of hot sauce. Braise for 3 hours, adding potatoes and carrots for the last hour. Proper flavour this time.

w.how: Peel and slice 6 Granny Smith apples and toss with 100g sugar and a teaspoon of cinnamon. Line a pie dish with sweet shortcrust, fill and cover with a pastry lid. Brush with beaten egg and bake at 190C for 50 minutes. Rest for an hour and serve with cream.

d.note: the quiet kitchen after evening prayers
d.how: Warm a big teapot with boiling water and tip it out. Add 6 English breakfast tea bags and fill with freshly boiled water. Steep for 4 minutes. Pour into plain white cups and set milk and sugar on the table so everyone can fix their own.
